title: Cell-free expression and NGS-powered substrate profiling reveal a thermostable metagenomic meganuclease from an extreme environment with novel specificity.
authors: Dorrazehi Gol Mohammad; Penner Matthew; Athanasiou Christina; Boursinhac Lise; Mobarec Juan Carlos et al.
abstract: As an alternative to historical enzyme isolation, metagenomic databases (e.g. MGnify) provide information on vast unculturable microbial diversity, including extreme environments, and constitute an enormous source of functional proteins. Conservative mining of these data by close sequence homology alone tends to identify merely different versions of known enzymes. Here we present a discovery strategy for meganucleases based on wider capture of less homologous enzymes in metagenomic databases, and incorporating metadata with their homology. We use cell-free expression to bypass host incompatibility and the need for purification, along with deep sequencing for experimental assessment of substrate specificity and cleavage pattern, thereby circumventing classical gel-based profiling. Specifically, we discovered the temperature-stable (>55°C), intron-encoded LAGLIDADG meganuclease I-MG11 that recognizes a GC-rich 17 base pair sequence to generate 4-nt palindromic 3'-overhangs-the first monomeric meganuclease to produce such overhangs. Co-folding models of I-MG11 bound to DNA provide a structural context for enzyme-DNA interactions, highlighting differences from other monomeric LAGLIDADG meganucleases (e.g. I-SceI) shaped by InDels (insertion-deletions) in the DNA-binding region that may cause specificity changes. Our strategy streamlines general bona fide identification and annotation of meganucleases, while the unique properties of I-MG11 expand the toolbox of molecular genome engineering.

title: Ultrasound-driven plant lipid vesicles amplify oncolytic virotherapy in colorectal cancer.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
authors: Li Baoyi; Li Xiaoyan; Deng Yuntian; Luo Yuting; Huang Yu et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy, and its treatment with oncolytic virotherapy is hindered by multiple delivery barriers and delayed therapeutic kinetics. To address these challenges, we developed a plant lipid-based vesicular system (P-M@Ce6-OVs) co-encapsulating oncolytic viruses (OVs) and sonosensitizer chlorin e6 (Ce6), enabling ultrasound (US)-guided, spatiotemporally controlled delivery to deep colorectal tumors. Under US exposure, the system enhanced mucus infiltration, tumor penetration, and lysosomal escape, while activating sonodynamic therapy to rapidly induce tumor ablation and compensate delayed viral oncolysis. In CRC mouse models, rectal administration of P-M@Ce6-OVs with US exposure achieved a 10.3-fold reduction in tumor burden compared with the control (without treatment), markedly outperforming monotherapies. Importantly, combination with αPD-L1 not only suppressed primary CRC and re-challenged tumors mimicking metastatic relapse, but also induced durable systemic immune protection. This triple combination further potentiated systemic and mucosal antitumor immunity, restoring cytotoxic T-cell function and reinforcing humoral and gut-localized immune responses. Notably, this treatment reshaped gut microbiota by enriching nucleoside-metabolizing bacteria (e.g., Lactobacillus taiwanensis) and altering microbial metabolic profiles, including the pathways related to pyrimidine catabolism and arachidonic acid oxidation. These microbiota and metabolic changes were associated with immune remodeling and tumor suppression. Collectively, this platform integrated US-enabled delivery, sonodynamic activation, and microbiome remodeling to synergistically suppress CRC and re-challenged tumor progression, amplifying virotherapy and antitumor immunity.

title: Whole-genome characterization and genomic stability of Mastadenovirus F40 and F41 in pediatric gastroenteritis.
authors: El-Shahidy Samar M; Zakaria Amira M; Ibrahim Mohanad A; Diab Atef M
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus types 40 and 41 (HAdV-40 and HAdV-41), belonging to the species Mastadenovirus faecale, are among the leading viral causes of acute gastroenteritis in children. Despite their clinical importance, whole-genome data on circulating strains remain limited. This study investigated the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of enteric Mastadenoviruses detected in children with acute gastroenteritis.
METHODS: A total of 632 stool specimens collected from hospitalized children with acute gastroenteritis were screened using a multiplex gastrointestinal real-time PCR panel. Five representative Mastadenovirus-positive samples underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing followed by genome reconstruction, phylogenetic analysis, pairwise sequence identity comparisons, genome-wide variant analysis, amino acid substitution profiling, and recombination analysis.
RESULTS: Mastadenoviruses were detected in 60/632 (9.5%) children, with the highest positivity observed among those aged 1-3 years. Co-infections occurred predominantly involving bacterial pathogens. Complete or near-complete genomes were recovered for all five sequenced isolates with high sequencing depth (2,806 × -34,120 ×), genome coverage (94.8%-100% at ≥ 10 ×), and nucleotide identity (99.19%-99.78%) relative to genotype-matched reference genomes. Phylogenetic analyses identified two HAdV-F40 and three HAdV-F41 isolates. Gene-specific phylogenies of the hexon, penton base, fiber, and DNA polymerase genes consistently confirmed genotype assignment. Pairwise sequence identity analysis and recombination analysis further supported classification with no evidence of intergenotypic recombination.
CONCLUSIONS: The sequenced enteric Mastadenovirus isolates exhibited high genomic conservation with limited within-genotype diversity and no detectable evidence of recent recombination. The concordance between gene-specific phylogenies, sequence identity analyses, and whole-genome comparisons supports the robustness of current molecular typing approaches and expands the limited genomic data available for circulating HAdV-F40 and HAdV-F41 strains.

title: Barrier-reinforcing hyaluronic acid-bilirubin nanodelivery of methylprednisolone for synergistic modulation of the intestinal barrier, immune system, and gut microbiome in colitis.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
authors: Lee Bom; Yoo Jeeeun; Jeon Hyeon-Jeong; Kim Yu Jeong; Cheng Xiaoliang et al.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by a self-reinforcing cycle of intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiome dysbiosis, and aberrant mucosal immune responses. Methylprednisolone (MPS) is a potent immunosuppressant used for IBD and may beneficially modulate the gut microbiome, but its systemic adverse effects and potential impairment of epithelial repair limit its therapeutic use. To overcome these limitations, we developed MPS-loaded hyaluronic acid-bilirubin nanoparticles (MPS@HABN), an oral nanomedicine designed to protect the intestinal epithelium from MPS-associated injury while enhancing the otherwise limited immune and microbiome modulation achieved by low-dose HABN. MPS@HABN limited premature drug release, increased MPS accumulation in the inflamed colon, and reduced systemic exposure and thymic involution. It also protected intestinal epithelial cells from MPS-associated and oxidative injury. In contrast, low-dose HABN alone showed limited immune and microbiome modulation, whereas free MPS caused intestinal barrier damage and systemic toxicity such as thymic involution. In a DSS-induced colitis model, MPS@HABN improved intestinal barrier function while enhancing immune and microbiome modulation, resulting in robust therapeutic efficacy beyond that of either component alone at a low HABN dose and a clinically relevant MPS dose. These findings support combining the complementary activities of MPS and HABN to overcome corticosteroid-associated epithelial injury and the limited efficacy of low-dose HABN, thereby helping to disrupt the pathological barrier-immune-microbiome cycle in colitis.

title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
authors: Chen Qi; Guo Chongye; Wang Ligui; Fan Guomei; Qu Xiaoli et al.
abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporating 12 597 transcriptomes across 148 species, gcPathogen 2.0 bridges the gap between gene carriage and functional expression for risk assessment. Furthermore, the platform integrates 285 925 pathogen metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) spanning human, animal, and environmental niches. Mapped across 68 Environment Ontology (ENVO) habitat categories, these MAGs enable comprehensive tracking of cross-habitat distribution of pathogens, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), virulence factors (VFs), and mobile genetic elements (MGEs). Leveraging a nonredundant reference set curated from seven public databases, we identified over 77 million AMPs belonging to >55 000 families across 438 bacterial pathogens. Finally, pan-genome analyses of 440 bacterial species map intraspecies functional distributions across core, accessory, and unique gene repertoires. gcPathogen 2.0 is publicly accessible at https://nmdc.cn/gcpathogen/.
